topic.name: The Coordinates of a Vector Relative to a Basis in Abstract Vector Spaces

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials:

\[ p_1(t)=1+t^2, \quad p_2(t)=1-t+2t^2, \quad q(t)=1-3t+4t^2. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t) \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (1+t^2)+ x_2 (1-t+2t^2 ) &=1-3t+4t^2 \\[3pt] (x_1+x_2)-x_2t+(x_1+2x_2)t^2 &=1-3t+4t^2. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+x_2 = 1 \\ -x_2 = -3 \\ x_1+2x_2 = 4. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{array} \right] & R_3 &:=R_3+(-1)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \end{array} \right] & R_3 &:=R_3+R_2 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+x_2 = 1 \\ -x_2 = -3. \end{cases} \]

From the second equation, we get $x_2 =3.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x_1+(3) = 1 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=-2. \]

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} -2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2=-2+3 = 1.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & -2 \\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} 0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -2 \\ 4 & 3\end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 2x_1-2x_2 \\ 3x_1+4x_2 & -2x_1+3x_2 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 4 \\ 20 & -2\end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1-2x_2 = 4 \\ 3x_1+4x_2 = 20 \\ -2x_1+3x_2 = -2. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 20 \\ -2 & 3 & -2 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & 20 \\ -2 & 3 & -2 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+\left(-\dfrac32\right)R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 7 & 14 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 2x_1-2x_2 = 4 \\ 7x_2 = 14\\ x_2= 2. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =2.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} 2x_1 - 2\cdot 2 &= 4 \\[3pt] 2x_1 &= 8\\[3pt] x_1 &=4. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = 4 + 2=6.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} 9 & -18 \\ 15 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ 3 & 0 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 9 & -18 \\ 15 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} 2x_1+ x_2 & -2x_1+2x_2 \\ 3x_1+x_2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} 9 & -18 \\ 15 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} 2x_1+ x_2=9 \\ -2x_1+2x_2 = -18 \\ 3x_1+x_2 = 15. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & -18 \\ 3 & 1 & 15 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 9 \\ -2 & 2 & -18 \\ 3 & 1 & 15 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 := R_2+R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+\left(-\dfrac32\right)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 2 & 1 & 9 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 \\ 0 & -\dfrac12 & \dfrac32 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} 2x_1 +x_2 = 9 \\ 3x_2 =-9\\ -\dfrac{x_2}2= \dfrac32. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =-3.$ From the first equation, we get

\begin{align*} 2x_1 +x_2 &= 9 \\[3pt] 2x_1 + (-3)&= 9 \\[3pt] x_1 &= 6. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ -3 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = 6+(-3)=3.$

question.text: Consider the following matrices: \[ B_1=\begin{bmatrix} 1 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B_2=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix}, \quad A=\begin{bmatrix} -1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \] If $\mathcal B = \{B_1,B_2\}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\{ B_1, B_2 \},$ and $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2 = $
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 B_1 +x_2 B_2 = A. \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 \begin{bmatrix}1 & -4 \\ 1 & 0 \end{bmatrix}+ x_2 \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix} \\[5pt] \begin{bmatrix} x_1+2x_2 & -4x_1-2x_2 \\ x_1-2x_2 & 0 \end{bmatrix} &= \begin{bmatrix} -1 & -8 \\ 7 & 0 \end{bmatrix}. \end{align*}

Equating the corresponding entries, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+2x_2 = -1 \\ -4x_1-2x_2 = -8 \\ x_1-2x_2 = 7. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & -2 & -8 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 \end{array} \right] && \begin{array}{l} R_2 :=R_2+4R_1 \\ R_3 :=R_3+ (-1)R_1 \end{array} \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 6 & -12 \\ 0 & -4 & 8 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now \[ \begin{cases} x_1+2x_2 = -1 \\ 6x_2 = -12\\ -4x_2= 8. \end{cases} \] From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =-2.$ From the first equation, we get \begin{align*} x_1 + 2\cdot (-2) &= -1 \\[3pt] x_1 &= -1+4 \\[3pt] x_1 &= 3. \end{align*}

Therefore, $[A]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ -2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2 = 3 + (-2)= 1.$

question.text:
Consider the following polynomials:

\[ p_1(t)=1+t, \quad p_2(t)=1-t+t^2, \quad q(t)=4+2t^2. \]

If $\mathcal{B}=\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \}$ is a basis of $\textrm{Span}\big\{ p_1(t), p_2(t) \big\},$ and $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{bmatrix},$ then $x_1+x_2=$
question.explanation:
We need to find $x_1$ and $x_2$ such that

\[ x_1 p_1(t)+x_2 p_2(t) = q(t) \]

Substituting the given information into the above equation, we get

\begin{align*} x_1 (1+t)+ x_2 (1-t+t^2 ) &=4+2t^2 \\[3pt] (x_1+x_2) +(x_1-x_2)t+x_2t^2 &=4+2t^2. \end{align*}

Equating the coefficients of $t$, we obtain

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+x_2 = 4 \\ x_1-x_2 = 0 \\ x_2 = 2. \end{cases} \]

The equations above give a linear system with the augmented matrix

\[ M= \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array} \right]. \]

Row-reducing the matrix using Gaussian elimination, we obtain the following:

\begin{align} M =& \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array} \right] & R_2 &:=R_2+(-1)R_1 \\[5pt] \sim & \left[ \begin{array}{cc|c} 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \end{array} \right] \end{align}

The system is now

\[ \begin{cases} x_1+x_2 = 4 \\ -2x_2 = -4\\ x_2=2. \end{cases} \]

From the second and third equations, we get $x_2 =2.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain

\[ x_1+(2) = 4 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad x_1=2. \]

Therefore, $[q(t)]_{\mathcal{B}}=\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}.$

Finally, $x_1+x_2=2+2 = 4.$
